void NpcM_DetectSlowdown(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float slowdownRate)
// If update rate has been set below 3, set it to 3.
// Check if the cycle count since last frame exceeds treshhold.
// If that's been happening for 10 frames, game is slowing down.
// Set the current camera as slow camera and set update rate lower.
// If the camera has been changed, or the last 40 frames have been above the
// slowdown treshhold, return update rate back up.
// Note: This doesn't mean the game is running OK yet - it might get undone once
// the update rate is back up to normal.
// SLOWDOWN_DETECTED variable only gets unset if the camera changed since last time.
// This is so that objects that have been culled out don't appear again -
// which might be what was keeping the framerate low in the first place.
cur->eye.x = Interpolate(ThonkZoomStartPoints[0], ThonkZoomEndPoints[0], THONK_ZOOM_FRAMES, TweenFrameCamera, EASING_TYPE_EASE_IN);

Messages.Name: AF_LINK20
Messages.Comment:
This is maybe the most subtle joke in the whole game.

All failure scenarios from this three-choice menu ("This info puts one thing into question") end with AF_LINK20_ALT, except for the one about Talon's poor taste in gifts. The difference is that AF_LINK20_ALT is worded such that Link admits that his argument was wrong ("[You're right,] But even so..."), whereas in this version (AF_LINK20), he doesn't admit that at all, and instead only tries to add more arguments to strengthen his case better ("But that's not the only thing!", ..."causes an even bigger problem"). In other words, Link still believes that his idea about Talon having bad taste in gifts is *correct*, and the only thing he's admitting to is that it was a bad idea to bring it up in court (both because it's irrelevant and because it offended everyone).

1. Its name must have a NpcM_ prefix (eg. NpcM_Function),
2. Must have at least two parameters: NpcMaker* and PlayState*. Up to 8 additional float arguments can be passed on from scripts.
3. If you plan to pass the result to scripts, the return type must be float
Examples of valid function signatures are thus, for example:
void NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float argument, float argument1)
The exception for this is functions which should run "On limb", their signature is as follows:
float NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* playState, s32 limbNumber, Gfx** dListPtr, Vec3f* translation, Vec3s* rotation, void* instance, Gfx** gfxP)
This function should return 0 if the limb is meant to be drawn, and 1 if it is not.
For "post limb" functions, the signature is the same, but some of the arguments might be NULL, and the function doesn't return anything.
For "Skin" models, only the limb number is available.
For others, everything but the translation is available.

CodeLines: To make NPC Maker able to use your function, it must have the following form:
1. Its name must have a NpcM_ prefix (eg. NpcM_Function),
2. Must have at least two parameters: NpcMaker* and PlayState*. Up to 8 additional float arguments can be passed on from scripts.
3. If you plan to pass the result to scripts, the return type must be float
Examples of valid function signatures are thus, for example:
void NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float argument, float argument1)
The exception for this is functions which should run "On limb", their signature is as follows:
float NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* playState, s32 limbNumber, Gfx** dListPtr, Vec3f* translation, Vec3s* rotation, void* instance, Gfx** gfxP)
This function should return 0 if the limb is meant to be drawn, and 1 if it is not.

Note 1: MUTOH9 is used if the player in the Link's Awakening savefile has gotten killed by the shopkeeper at least once (by re-entering the store), and MUTOH9A is used if they haven't been killed yet.

Note 2: It's a bit hard to tell, but when the shopkeeper says certain intimidating statements such as this one, he drops his Scottish accent and speaks in normal English. (Other places where this happens will be marked in the translator notes.)

Note 3: "The ultimate price" is an English phrase that normally means death, and that *is* what he means here too, though in his press dialogue, he'll lie and say he was only referring to the curse.

Note 4: It's also something the shopkeeper says in his Link's Awakening dialogue just before he kills you ("I wasn't kidding when I said pay! Now, you'll pay the ultimate price!!"). If possible, please reference the corresponding Link's Awakening localization for an equivalent phrase.

CodeLines: To make NPC Maker able to use your function, it must have the following form:
1. Its name must have a NpcM_ prefix (eg. NpcM_Function),
2. Must have at least two parameters: NpcMaker* and PlayState*. Up to 8 additional float arguments can be passed on from scripts.
3. If you plan to pass the result to scripts, the return type must be float
Examples of valid function signatures are thus, for example:
void NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float argument, float argument1)
The exception for this is functions which should run "On limb", their signature is as follows:
float NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* playState, s32 limbNumber, Gfx** dListPtr, Vec3f* translation, Vec3s* rotation, void* instance, Gfx** gfxP)
This function should return 0 if the limb is meant to be drawn, and 1 if it is not.

Canonically, the Wind Fish isn't considered to be a member of the Zelda series's "Leviathan" species (https://zeldawiki.wiki/wiki/Leviathan) -- or at least, there's no specific evidence of it. Because of that, I've seen players, upon reading this line, wonder if we're establishing it as a fact here, as part of our modified canon.

The truth is that, no, the owl is just using the word in its generic sense of "a large sea animal" (https://www.merriam-webster.com/dictionary/leviathan).

Messages.Name: About_Tutorial
Messages.Comment:
General notes for all of these "about" messages:

- Put the translated song title on the first line (red), the original English title in parentheses on the second line (white), and the composer name in parentheses on the third line (blue). See French for examples.

- If you don't know the official title of a Nintendo or Capcom song in your language, feel free to ask us about it in the Discord server. We can help look for official song title localizations.

- If the translation of a dialog box is too big to fit in one box, you can split it into two. Try to find a natural place in the sentence to split it at.

- Due to the 1280-byte limit on message sizes, some of these text sequences are split into multiple messages, ending with "_a", "_b", etc. The "_b" and "_c" messages are at the bottom of the message list rather than next to the "_a" ones, for technical reasons.

- If your translation of a message goes past the 1280-byte limit (there'll be an obvious error message if this happens), we may need to split it into more messages. Ask Skawo or RoadrunnerWMC for help with that.

1. Its name must have a NpcM_ prefix (eg. NpcM_Function),
2. Must have at least two parameters: NpcMaker* and PlayState*. Up to 8 additional float arguments can be passed on from scripts.
3. If you plan to pass the result to scripts, the return type must be float

void NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float argument, float argument1)

CodeLines: To make NPC Maker able to use your function, it must have the following form:
1. Its name must have a NpcM_ prefix (eg. NpcM_Function),
2. Must have at least two parameters: NpcMaker* and PlayState*. Up to 8 additional float arguments can be passed on from scripts.
3. If you plan to pass the result to scripts, the return type must be float
Examples of valid function signatures are thus, for example:
void NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* play, float argument, float argument1)
The exception for this is functions which should run "On limb", their signature is as follows:
float NpcM_Function(NpcMaker* npc, PlayState* playState, s32 limbNumber, Gfx** dListPtr, Vec3f* translation, Vec3s* rotation, void* instance, Gfx** gfxP)
This function should return 0 if the limb is meant to be drawn, and 1 if it is not.
For "post limb" functions, the signature is the same, but some of the arguments might be NULL, and the function doesn't return anything.
For "Skin" models, only the limb number is available.
For others, everything but the translation is available.
Warning; When using these functions from scripts, make sure
